outline.unique_angle: A concrete first-person decision rule from a working nurse — a named 'put the phone down' checklist of specific time-critical presentations (cardiac, airway, sudden mental-status change) where reaching for any AI tool is itself the clinical error. Competitors argue AI 'shouldn't replace nurses' in the abstract; none give nurses an actionable bedside trigger list for when NOT to touch the tool, nor the post-event boundary (AI fine for the handoff write-up, never for the live call).

warnings: AI Overview almost certainly present for the broad 'limitations/disadvantages of AI in nursing' head term and will steal informational clicks — only target the narrower 'when NOT to / cases that need hands' framing where depth + first-person authority wins.

Top-10 SERP is dominated by high-DR institutional/union/.gov pages (NNU DR~70, WSNA DR~50, PMC/.gov DR~90) for the BROAD term; ranking for the head term is unrealistic for a new domain. The long-tail 'when nurses should NOT rely on AI' framing has near-zero exact-match competition, hence the low KD estimate — but KD is high-uncertainty because authority sites bleed into the long-tail SERP.
